units.source_text: 笔迹富有古风。

en.t: The handwriting had an old-fashioned elegance.

units.source_text: 源氏看了，不断地微笑，一时不忍释手。

en.t: Genji looked at it, kept smiling, and for a while could not bear to put it down.

units.source_text: 紫姬不知道他为了何事，回转头来注视。

en.t: Lady Murasaki, not knowing what had so absorbed him, turned back and looked at him.

units.source_text: 末摘花犒赏使者如此微薄，源氏觉得扫兴，并且有伤他的体面，脸上显出不快之色。

en.t: The reward Suetsumuhana had given the messenger was so meager that Genji felt disappointed, thought it damaged his dignity, and showed displeasure on his face.

units.source_text: 使者知趣，连忙悄悄地退去。

en.t: The messenger understood the situation and quickly withdrew in silence.

units.source_text: 身边众侍女见此光景，互相私语窃笑。

en.t: The ladies-in-waiting nearby saw what had happened and whispered to one another, secretly laughing.

units.source_text: 末摘花如此一味守旧，专长于使人扫兴之事，使得源氏无法对付。

en.t: Suetsumuhana was so stubbornly old-fashioned and so skilled at dampening people's spirits that Genji did not know how to deal with her.

units.source_text: 关于她那首诗，他说道：“她倒是个道地的诗人呢。

en.t: Speaking of her poem, he said, "She really is a genuine poet.

units.source_text: 作起古风诗歌来，离不开‘唐装’‘濡袖’等恨语。

en.t: When composing old-fashioned poems, she cannot do without plaintive phrases such as 'Chinese robe' and 'wet sleeves.'

units.source_text: 其实我也是此种人。

en.t: In truth, I am that sort of person too.

units.source_text: 墨守古法，不受新语影响，这也是难得的。

en.t: It is rare, after all, to cling to the old methods and remain untouched by new expressions.

units.source_text: 群贤集会之时，例如在御前，特地举行诗会之时，吟咏友情，必须用一定的字眼；

en.t: When distinguished people gather, for example at a poetry meeting specially held before His Majesty, poems on friendship must use certain fixed words;

units.source_text: 吟咏相思，则必在第三句中用‘冤家’等字样。

en.t: and when composing on longing in love, one must put words such as 'cruel beloved' in the third line.

units.source_text: 古人以为必须如此，读起来才顺口。”

en.t: People of old believed it had to be done this way for the poem to sound smooth when read."

units.source_text: 说罢哈哈大笑。

en.t: Having said this, he burst into loud laughter.

units.source_text: 后来又说：“他们必须熟读种种诗歌笔记，牢记诗歌中所咏种种名胜，然后从其中选取语词来作诗。

en.t: Later he added, "They must read all kinds of poetry notebooks closely, memorize the many famous places celebrated in poems, and then choose words from them to compose their own verses.

units.source_text: 因此惯用的语句，大都千篇一律，无甚变化。

en.t: As a result, the phrases they habitually use are mostly all the same, with hardly any variation.

units.source_text: 末摘花的父亲常陆亲王曾经用纸屋纸写了一册诗歌笔记。

en.t: Suetsumuhana's father, Prince Hitachi, once wrote a volume of poetry notes on Kamiyagami paper.

units.source_text: 末摘花要我读，将此书送给我。

en.t: Suetsumuhana wanted me to read it and sent the book to me.

units.source_text: 其中全是诗歌作法的规则，还指出许多必须避免之弊病。

en.t: It was full of rules for composing poetry and also pointed out many faults that had to be avoided.

units.source_text: 我于此道本不擅长，看了这许多清规戒律，反而动手不得了。

en.t: I was never skilled in that art, and after seeing so many strict rules, I became even less able to begin.

units.source_text: 厌烦起来，把书送还了她。

en.t: I grew tired of it and returned the book to her.

units.source_text: 她是深通此道的人，现在这一首还算是通俗的呢。”

en.t: She is someone deeply versed in this art, and this present poem is actually one of her more accessible ones."

units.source_text: 对末摘花的诗虽然赞誉，但对她父亲的笔记不以为然。

en.t: Although he praised Suetsumuhana's poem, he had little regard for her father's notebook.

units.source_text: 紫姬认真地说：“你为什么送还了她呢？

en.t: Lady Murasaki said earnestly, "Why did you return it to her?

units.source_text: 应该抄下来，将来给我们的小女儿看。

en.t: You should have copied it out and shown it someday to our little daughter.

units.source_text: 我的书橱里也藏着这一类古书，但都被书蠹蛀破了。

en.t: I have old books of that sort stored in my bookcase too, but they have all been eaten through by bookworms.

units.source_text: 不悉此道的人看了，不知道写着些什么呢。”

en.t: Someone unfamiliar with this art would look at them and have no idea what was written there."

units.source_text: 源氏说：“我们女儿的教育上用不着这些东西。

en.t: Genji said, "Our daughter's education has no need for such things.

units.source_text: 凡为女子者，特别专精一种学问，是不相宜的。

en.t: For a woman, it is unsuitable to become especially absorbed in one field of learning.

units.source_text: 但倘对一切文艺一概不懂，也是不好的。

en.t: But it is also not good for her to know nothing at all of the arts.

units.source_text: 总之，只要心地稳重，思虑周密，对付万事自有主意，便是好女子了。”

en.t: In short, if she has a steady heart, thinks carefully, and has judgment of her own in handling everything, she will be a fine woman."

units.source_text: 他只管谈论，并不想答复末摘花的赠诗。

en.t: He went on talking and did not seem inclined to answer Suetsumuhana's poem.

units.source_text: 紫姬劝道：“她诗中说‘欲返春衫’，你不答复她，怕不好意思吧。”

en.t: Lady Murasaki urged him, "Her poem says that she wishes to return the spring robe. If you do not answer her, it may be rather embarrassing."

units.source_text: 源氏向来不肯辜负人家好意，就立刻写答诗。

en.t: Genji, who never liked to slight another person's kindness, immediately wrote a reply poem.

units.source_text: 他漫不经心地写道：

en.t: He wrote casually:
